exposure: timing of conspicuity in utero (mid-second trimester, third trimester, or not seen prenatally)
outcome: histological diagnosis (primary lung tumors vs. developmental abnormalities)
cohort: The study included 135 fetuses/neonates diagnosed with congenital lung lesions (4 tumors and 131 malformations) at a university mother and child center over a 10-year period (2005-2015).
finding: Congenital lung lesions not visible on mid-second-trimester ultrasound are highly suggestive of primary lung tumors, differentiating them from developmental pulmonary abnormalities which are typically detected during this period.
